jobs.title: Traffic & Marketing Coordinator
jobs.desc:
Job description

The Traffic & Marketing Coordinator keeps work moving at Bish. Their primary job is traffic: making sure every project is complete before it reaches the Design team and production, planning the time it needs, and tracking it through to handoff so Account Managers and clients never get surprised. Their second job is marketing administration: running the day-to-day publishing, email, website, asset library, and trade show logistics that keep Bish’s own marketing on schedule.

Both halves call for the same strengths: organization, follow-through, clear communication, and the judgment to spot a problem before it becomes one. This is not a design role. It exists so designers spend their time designing.

TRAFFIC COORDINATION (primary — approx. 60%)
• Own the handoff between Account Management and Design: review every new project request against a standard brief and checklist — scope, specs, dimensions, quantities, materials, copy, brand assets, approvals, and due dates — before it enters the design queue.
• Return incomplete requests to the Account Manager with a clear list of what is missing. A project does not move into design or production until its brief is complete.
• With the Design lead, estimate and allocate the hours each project needs; build and maintain the team schedule so capacity, conflicts, and rush requests are visible to everyone.
• Track every active project from brief through production handoff — status, next step, owner, and due date — and update Account Managers before they have to ask, especially when something is at risk.
• Confirm files, proofs, and client approvals are final before work is released to production.
• Run a short weekly work-in-progress review with Design and Account Management, and publish a schedule everyone can see.
• Manage rush requests through a defined process: assess the impact on committed work and escalate trade-offs to the COO rather than quietly reshuffling the schedule.
• Keep project records — briefs, versions, approvals, and final files — organized and archived so past work can be found and reused.
• Report monthly on turnaround times and the recurring causes of delay (for example, incomplete briefs or late approvals) so the process keeps improving.

MARKETING ADMINISTRATION (secondary — approx. 40%)
Working with the Director of Brand & Marketing, who sets direction and approves all content:
• Schedule and publish social and LinkedIn content from approved designs and copy; maintain the content calendar and pull monthly analytics.
• Handle day-to-day community monitoring and responses per guidelines, and keep an eye on competitors’ social media and websites.
• Build, test, and deploy Mailchimp campaigns from approved designs and copy; manage lists and report on opens, clicks, and basic performance.
• Make routine website updates through the CMS — copy, imagery, and new case studies — from approved content.
• Own the asset library: tag every photo and file by client, project, status (prototype / in production / in-market), and shareability (internal only / client-approved / approved after a date), with consistent naming and folders so anyone can find an asset in seconds.
• Because traffic sees every project, flag work worth photographing at each stage, schedule the photography, and confirm with Account Managers what has shipped and what is cleared to show.
• Maintain the template and deck library so ready-made materials can be pulled quickly, and route marketing requests through the same intake process used for client work.
• Coordinate logistics for SHOP! Marketplace and other trade shows: show calendar, exhibitor deadlines and service orders, shipping featured displays and booth materials to and from the show, booth inventory between events, and on-site setup and teardown support.

Priorities: traffic comes first day to day, because production deadlines are client commitments;

Oath is the strategic giving platform designed to help donors maximize the impact of their contributions by guiding them to the races and causes where their dollars can make the greatest impact. You'll run the channels that bring new grassroots donors into Oath and turn existing donors into recruiters. Your mission is to grow Oath's donor base through paid media and peer-to-peer programs while building a community of donors who share Oath with their networks. Sticker Shuttle is a small, fast-growing custom sticker company in Denver. We run a tech-driven shop and share the real, unfiltered story of building it with millions of people every month. We currently average over 4.5 million Instagram views per month. We need someone who can take our social to the next level and keep it consistent every single day.

This isn't a corporate marketing job. There's no brand committee, no approval chain and no decks. You'll be in the shop with us, phone or camera in hand, turning what happens here into content that stops the scroll.

**What You'll Do**

* Plan, shoot, edit and post short-form content every day for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Threads and X.
* Write and structure videos around a hook that grabs viewers in the first 1–2 seconds, a payoff that keeps them watching, and a clear call to action.
* Spot trends, sounds and formats early and adapt them to Sticker Shuttle quickly.
* Own the weekly content calendar. Come in Monday with ideas and a plan, and talk it through with Justin.
* Keep Instagram Stories active every day, build story and post automations, and respond to comments and DMs to build our community.
* Track performance (views, retention, shares, follows, clicks), report what's working each week, and do more of it.
* Clip long-form footage into short-form when we film it.
* Update ManyChat automations when we run deals or promotions. Turn followers into customers.

**What We're Looking For**

* You've helped grow an account, either your own, a client's or a brand's, and you can show the numbers.
* You understand viral structure: hooks, retention, payoff, CTAs, pacing and captions. You can explain why a video worked.
* You pay attention content producers who teach about hooks, meat, CTA's, story telling, and other processes to improve organic content.
* You edit fast in Edits and CapCut, and you use AI tools to move faster, not to replace creativity. We trust the creativity humans provide more.
* You know authenticity beats production value for this kind of content.
* You're comfortable on camera, or happy to direct others in front of it.
* You're self-directed. You can see what's happening in the shop and turn it into content without being told what to film.
* You've a good understanding of what gets someone to stop scrolling and watch a video.
* You're curious about business, entrepreneurship and building something real.
* You're reliable, on time and own your results.

**What You Don't Need**

* A degree or fancy gear. We have the equipment. We have phones, laptops, cameras, etc.

* Sticker knowledge. We'll teach you what matters.

Send a short note about yourself and why this role fits you. Include links to accounts you've grown or videos you've made, plus your best-performing post and why you think it worked. We're humans, not robots, so just show us how you think.

jobs.title: Marketing Manager
jobs.desc:
We are a commercial cleaning master franchise serving Oregon and Washington. We want to be *the* name facility and property managers think of when they think “reliable, elevated cleaning” in the Pacific Northwest.

To do that, we are building a **Stratus Marketing Machine**: a repeatable system that turns customer proof, content, and offers into leads and brand equity without depending on the founder.

You will be the person who owns and runs that machine.

Your mission (what you actually own)

Your scorecard will be simple and visible:

* **Qualified demand**
* X new qualified opportunities per month from facility / property managers in OR–WA (number set with you based on current baseline).
* **Local visibility**
* Growth in organic + direct traffic to our territory pages.
* # of priority cities where we rank in the top 3 map pack for “commercial cleaning + city.”
* **Reputation & brand**
* New 5-star Google reviews per month across franchisees.
* Average rating above 4.7+.
* Consistent “Stratus Clean PNW = elevated, low-drama commercial cleaning” message across channels.

If these numbers move in the right direction, you’re winning. If they stall, you own the plan to fix it.

What you’ll do

* Design and run the **Stratus Clean PNW Marketing Machine**: build and maintain checklists that constantly generate customer proof, content, and campaigns we can use across SEO, social, email, and sales collateral.
* Own **local SEO**: Google Business Profiles, on-site SEO, location pages, citation management, and reporting for our key markets.
* Build and enforce a **review-generation system** across franchisees with clear scripts, touchpoints, and goals.
* Create and manage a **simple content calendar** for LinkedIn and other relevant platforms, focused on case studies, proof, and offers for facility managers (not vanity posts).
* Coordinate with any external vendors (paid media, web) as the internal owner: set targets, review performance, and make keep/kill/scale decisions.
* Report weekly and monthly on your scorecard, insights, and next experiments.
* Work cross-functionally with franchise owners and sales to ensure what we promise in marketing matches what we deliver, reinforcing our brand flywheel.

You’re a fit if

* 5–8+ years in **hands-on local marketing** (SEO, Google Business, social/content) for service or multi-location businesses.
* You can show **before/after examples** of moving rankings, traffic, and leads – not just followers.
* You think in **systems**, not one-off campaigns: you like checklists, playbooks, and repeatable processes.
* You’re comfortable being both **strategic and scrappy**: one hour you’re in GA/Search Console, the next hour you’re filming a quick on-site case study video.
* You’re data-driven: you can build a simple dashboard, read it, and change behavior based on it.
* You act like an owner: you want your work tied to real business outcomes, not activity.

What success looks like

**In 90 days:**

* Clear baseline metrics and a simple dashboard live.
* Review system installed and producing consistent 5-star reviews.
* Priority city list defined and first ranking lifts in motion.
* Weekly content and proof cadence running without founder involvement.

**In 12 months:**

* Stratus Clean PNW is the most visible and best-reviewed commercial cleaner in our core metros.
* Our lead flow is measurably stronger and more predictable, and the marketing machine runs off checklists you built.

Compensation & process

* Competitive base salary in line with experienced marketing managers in Portland/Seattle, plus **performance-based bonus** tied to your scorecard.
* Hiring process: short application → 20-minute intro call → **paid test project** (audit + 90-day plan for 2 cities) → panel interview.

If you want to own the marketing machine for a growing regional brand and have your scorecard tied directly to visible market dominance, we’d like to talk.

Pay: $64,700.00 - $78,100.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)

**Are you ready to level up your social media management skills?**

As the social media manager at Ironside, you manage 9-10 social media accounts based on a predetermined strategy provided by the Brand Manager. You are responsible for creating the content, scheduling the posts, and utilizing growth strategies on platform.

**What the work actually is**

Our social product is already written. Clients do not buy “posts.” They buy an account built around their business goals. You will run that system - content mix, quarterly capture, monthly reporting.

* Follow the strategy for each account against a defined business goal
* Run content capture days at client sites: restaurants mid-service, roofing jobs in August, showrooms with bad light. You direct, shoot, light, and record sound using iphone and professional equipment as needed.
* Capture enough usable video and photos to support an account for one to three months.
* Shoot photography at a quality we can also use in print, on the website, and in ads — product, food, crew portraits, location, before-and-afters.
* Edit vertical video with clean audio. Roughly 80% of what we produce. Color and finish your own stills.
* Graphic design to brand standards and social media trends using Canva or other appropriate design platforms.
* Write copy for posts, captions, and more in the client's brand voice.
* Schedule, submit posts for review, edit, and coordinate for approvals directly with the client.
* Build and maintain a content library and a 90-day calendar for each client.
* Report monthly in plain English: the handful of numbers that match the goal, what moved them, and what changes next.

**Who this is for**

* Two-plus years running social accounts professionally — agency, in-house, or on your own. We care what the accounts did, not what your title was.
* Real experience in this market valuable. You have lived on the Treasure Coast and worked with businesses here.
* You are a photographer and a videographer. DSLR or iPhone, and you know when each is the right call.
* You have a good eye for graphic design and composition.
* You are outgoing and enjoy working with clients.
* You can shoot a full day alone and come back with volume. No second shooter. This is the single hardest part of the job.
* You edit your own work, video and stills.
* Comfortable in Claude, Photoshop, Lightroom, Canva, and Figma. Strong in at least a few of them.
* Organized enough for nine accounts at once: capture calendars, libraries, posting schedules, campaign checks, reporting. Nothing slips quietly.
* Meta Business Suite, Instagram, Facebook. Working knowledge of TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and Nextdoor.

**What this job is not**

* Not remote. Not hybrid.

**What you get**

* Health benefits and paid time off.
* Equipment provided.
* A full creative shop down the hall: brand, design, web, video, print.

**How to apply**

Send the following.

1. Three accounts you have run. Handles or links. A few sentences each: what the business needed, what you built, what it produced.

2. Two vertical videos and five photographs, all shot and edited by you. Not a highlight reel — individual pieces, with a line about what you were working around. At least one video should have someone talking, so we can hear your audio.

Ironside Press, 1001 20th Place, Vero Beach, Florida. Serving the Treasure Coast since 1989. Print. Mail. Brand. Design. Web. Video. And now, social — run with the same standard as everything else that leaves this building.

**Position & Company Overview**

ReSupply is looking for an experienced SEO Manager to help shape and deliver the marketing strategy that will reinvent and forever change the supply chain of charitable contributions in the U.S., helping turn household goods into emergency relief for those in need. If you're excited about leveraging organic search to solve meaningful problems while making a tangible social impact, we'd love to talk to you.

As the SEO Manager, you will own organic search at ReSupply from top to bottom, including technical health, local and service-area pages, content, and how we show up in AI-generated answers. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports, making it ideal for someone who enjoys setting the strategic plan as well as executing the work to ensure ReSupply is the answer people find when they need to donate goods.

You'll shape the SEO roadmap, prioritizing the fixes and content that actually drive bookings and revenue over vanity metrics. You'll work closely with our paid search team, web designer, and engineering team to improve the experiences and visibility that power ReSupply's business. Because you'll be working across technical SEO, content generation, and emerging AI search trends, you'll have the opportunity to understand how our digital presence connects donors with charities and help build a marketing engine that scales with the company.

Our small, tight-knit team is seeking a candidate who will work closely with us at our Downtown Boston headquarters. We do our best work when we can innovate together in an open, collaborative environment. Our culture is built on thinking disruptively, obsessing over adding value, and supporting one another as we strive to Make Giving Simple – and have fun doing it!

Click to learn how ReSupply is forever changing charitable giving: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AVW60dsKJq0&t=6s

**What you'll do**

* **Own the SEO roadmap** and decide what matters most. We'd rather you fix the five things that move bookings than the fifty things a crawler flags.
* **Keep the site technically healthy:** Crawling, indexing, redirects, canonicals, site speed, and structured data. Write tickets clear enough that an engineer can ship them without a follow-up meeting.
* **Make our local pages worth landing on.** We serve thousands of zip codes, and someone searching for couch donation pickup in Tampa should find a page that actually helps someone in Tampa.
* **Work out how ReSupply shows up in AI search** (Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and whatever launches next month) and build a plan for it based on testing, not hype.
* **Turn keyword and intent research into content briefs**, and write or edit priority pages yourself when that's faster.
* **Report on what organic search is actually worth to us:** bookings and revenue, with branded and non-branded split out. Rankings are useful clues, not the goal.
* **Earn links and mentions the honest way**, through useful content and our charity partnerships.
* **Borrow from paid search.** Our ad accounts are full of real search terms and conversion data, and you're welcome to all of it.

**How AI fits into this job**

Search is changing faster than it has in twenty years, and more and more people get their answer before they ever click a link. We want someone who finds that interesting rather than threatening. We use AI every day on the marketing team, and we'd expect you to as well. In practice, that means:

* **Using AI to speed up the heavy lifting**, like clustering keywords, drafting briefs, writing regex and scripts, and digging through crawl exports. We'll ask you to show us how you do it.
* **Knowing the difference between AI-assisted content that helps people and mass-produced pages that get a site demoted.** With thousands of local pages, that line matters a lot here.
* **Measuring AI visibility the way you'd measure anything else, with data:** referral traffic from AI tools, how often we get cite

ReSupply is looking for an adaptable, data-driven Growth Marketing Manager to help shape and deliver the marketing strategy that will reinvent and forever change the supply chain of charitable contributions in the U.S., helping turn household goods into emergency relief for those in need. If you're excited about leveraging email, organic social, and influencer partnerships to make a tangible social impact, we'd love to talk to you.

As the Growth Marketing Manager, you will own three of ReSupply's channels from top to bottom: email, our organic social accounts, and our affiliate and influencer partnerships. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports, making it ideal for someone who enjoys setting the strategic plan as well as executing the work - heavily supported by modern AI tools - to ensure people see ReSupply as the easiest way to give their stuff a second life.

You'll shape the roadmap for these three channels, prioritizing the campaigns and partnerships that actually drive incremental bookings and revenue over vanity metrics like likes and follower counts. You'll work closely with our marketing team, sales, and customer success to improve the experiences and visibility that power ReSupply's business. Because you'll be working across email automation, social content, and partner negotiation, you'll have the opportunity to understand how our digital presence connects donors with charities and help build a marketing engine that scales with the company.

Our culture is built on thinking disruptively, obsessing over adding value, and supporting one another as we strive to Make Giving Simple – and have fun doing it!

Email (you'll learn a lot of this on the job)

* Plan campaigns around the moments people actually donate: moving season, spring cleaning, college move-out, and year-end giving.
* QA everything before it goes out. Nobody should get a "finish your booking" email the day after their pickup.

Affiliate and influencer partnerships

* Take over our affiliate program. Right now that's one partnership, Momfluence, which connects us with mom creators. We'd like it to be a lot more than one.
* Find and test new partners and platforms, from creators to referral partners like movers and realtors, and negotiate terms that make sense for the business.
* Track every partner to verified bookings and true cost per booking, and work with finance on commissions.

Organic social

* Run ReSupply's social channels with a plan built around what drives visits and bookings, not follower counts.
* Turn what we already have (pickups, charity partner stories, customer reviews, creator content) into posts, working with our designer and AI tools to produce them.
* Keep an eye on comments and DMs, and send booking or service issues to our support team.

Across all three

* Measure what's actually incremental. Use holdout groups, test-and-control splits, and clean tracking to separate new revenue from bookings that would have happened anyway.
* Report monthly on what each channel drove and what it cost, with results de-duplicated across channels and checked against paid media.
* Recommend where the next dollar and the next hour should go, even when the answer is "less of something we like."

**Content Marketing Manager**

For over 100 years, we've restored Steinways that become treasured family heirlooms. In a world moving faster than ever, we blend old-world craftsmanship with exceptional service so families can slow down and enjoy music together. We're hiring a Content Marketing Manager to share this craft and tell stories that matter through the videos, livestreams, web pages, emails, and campaigns that help more piano lovers find their dream Steinway.

**About Lindeblad**

We're a family business that sells pre-owned and restored Steinway pianos to buyers nationwide, led by Todd Lindeblad, our fourth-generation owner.

* Our showroom is in Pine Brook, NJ, and our Restoration Center is in Dover, NJ.
* We restore and sell more Steinways than anyone in the country, with 25 craftsmen and over 300 years of combined experience.
* Our pianos are in the homes of concert artists and Steinway artists, and of Taylor Swift, Stephen Colbert, and more.
* We're a team of 35 people.

**The Job**

We’ve built marketing playbooks that work, and we’re looking for someone to run them and make them better. The role covers long-form videos filmed with Todd and our craftsmen, a monthly livestream, SEO pages and blogs based on the video topics, and the promotions we run throughout the year. You’ll start from a library of Claude skills (saved instructions) we’ve built for video scripts, emails, captions, and launches, so every draft begins from a strong first version that you shape and improve. As you learn what works, you’ll help decide what we change and test next.

**What You'll Own**

* **Long-form video and its web page**
* Write video scripts from our topic list, which is built from what Steinway buyers search for. The goal is to improve SEO/AEO and organic search traffic.
* Plan each shoot, film Todd and our craftsmen, and give our video editor revision notes until each video is ready to post
* Build the SEO/AEO page on our website that goes with each video
* Outcome**:** launch 2 new videos a month, each with its own SEO landing page
* **The monthly livestream and our giveaway**
* Script and produce a monthly livestream with Todd, and run the camera (we shoot on an iPhone)
* Run our giveaway from a documented playbook: the entry page, the sweepstakes administrator, the qualifying questions, and the winner selection
* Outcome**:** a livestream every month on schedule, and giveaway leads handed to our sales team
* **Promotions**
* Launch each promotion end to end from our playbook: landing pages, site banners, website chat, the email sequence in Pardot, campaign tracking in Salesforce, and taking it all down when it ends
* Outcome**:** every promotion on the calendar launches and ends on its dates, with results recorded and used to improve future promotions
* **Website updates and landing page tests**
* Update pages and build landing page tests with Claude Code; our web designer polishes them
* No coding background required.
* Outcome**:** tests and pages live on schedule
* **Organic social, starting around month 3**
* Keep our 7 social channels posting, using our AI-assisted caption and review process to write and schedule posts
* Study trends and how our past posts performed, and use what you learn to improve the content and grow engagement
* Outcome**:** 5 posts a day with no gaps
* **Lead volume KPIs**
* Track our lead volume and other marketing KPIs every week
* Outcome**:** lead volume KPIs tracked and current every week

**Your First Year**

* **By 60 days:** you run livestream production, ship 2 long-form videos a month with their pages, and track lead volume KPIs every week

Oritain is a global leader in forensic origin verification of products and raw materials. With offices in Washington D.C, Auckland, Dunedin, London, Paris and Singapore our vision is to be the source of truth in global supply chains.

This is a newly created role and our first dedicated marketing hire focused on the US. You’ll take our global marketing strategy and bring it to life in the US, building a regional approach from the ground up as we grow.

It’s a hands-on, commercially focused role with a genuine balance of field marketing and account-based marketing. Working side by side with our US Sales team, you’ll plan and deliver the events, executive engagement and targeted account programs that build pipeline with our priority customers. Your focus will be mainly on cotton, with the opportunity to help launch newer commodities such as timber and leather as they scale.

You’ll be based on-site in our Washington D.C. office, alongside some of our most experienced commercial colleagues, and part of a collaborative global marketing team.

jobs.desc:
**Social Media & Content Manager**

**Role snapshot**

* **Title:** Senior Social Media & Content Manager
* **Team:** Pure Brands (brand and wholesale marketing)
* **Reports to:** Marketing Manager
* **Location:** Lansing, Michigan — hybrid, with on-site shoots at our cultivation and processing facilities
* **Type:** Full-time, exempt
* **Compensation:** $75,000–$90,000 base salary, plus benefits

**The opportunity**

We're looking for a creator-strategist who wants to own a brand's entire social and content presence: the plan, the shoot, the edit, the post, and the results. You'll be the eye behind every frame and the voice behind every caption for Pure Brands, in one of the most regulated and creatively demanding categories there is.

We're a lean team that moves fast. There's no agency to hand work off to and a short path from idea to published. You'll set the direction, pick up the camera, and be trusted to make work that stands next to the best brands in cannabis.

***What you'll own***

**Strategy and planning**

* Build and run the social and content strategy for Pure Brands, tied to clear goals for consumers and wholesale partners.
* Own the monthly content calendar and content bank. Align priorities with the Marketing Manager, then run with it.
* Audit what's working across our channels and competitors, and decide where to double down and what to cut.

**Content creation: photo, video, and copy**

* Concept, shoot, and edit all photo and video in-house: product, lifestyle, cultivation and process, events, and people.
* Make short-form video (Reels, TikTok, Shorts) a core weekly output, with longer pieces when the story calls for it.
* Write sharp, on-brand captions and copy.
* Run the shoot schedule, gear, and asset library so every piece is organized and reusable.

**Channels and community**

* Lead with Instagram, with Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and LinkedIn as priority secondaries. Expand to other platforms when the audience is there.
* Engage the community daily through comments, DMs, Stories, and collaborations so the brand feels active and human.
* Build relationships with creators and partners, and bring them into the content.

**Partner and brand support**

* Create content that helps retail partners sell our products: launch kits, menu-ready imagery, and shareable social assets.
* Collaborate with peers on the other brands in our portfolio.

**Results and compliance**

* Track performance weekly and report monthly: reach, engagement, saves and shares, profile and website traffic, follower growth, leads, and conversions.
* Turn the data into decisions: what to make more of, what to stop, and what to test next.
* Keep every post compliant with Michigan cannabis marketing rules and each platform's policies, protecting both the accounts and the licenses

***What success looks like***

**First 30 days**

* Audit every channel, the existing content library, and the competitive landscape.
* Get on-site at our facilities, meet the team, and start shooting.
* Deliver a 90-day strategy with goals, channel priorities, and a content mix.

**By 60 days**

* The content calendar is fully running on a steady weekly rhythm of Reels, photo, and Stories.
* A reporting dashboard is live, with a baseline for every KPI.

**By 90 days**

* Reach, engagement, and follower growth are measurably up against baseline.
* The content bank runs two to four weeks ahead.
* At least one partner content kit is live with retail accounts.

**Ongoing-What good looks like**

*Publishing rhythm--*

Daily feed posts and Stories on Instagram and Facebook; 3+ Reels a week

*Audience growth--*

100+ new, relevant followers a week across Instagram and Facebook

*Engagement--*

Daily community management and a rising engagement rate

*Business impact--*

A clear line from social to website traffic, leads, and partner sell-through

*Reporting--*

A weekly pulse and a monthly recap with insights and next moves

**Who you are**

* 3+ years owning social me

========================

Dallas, TX

**About the role**
==================

This role supports the development and execution of media plans by preparing and maintaining essential planning materials, campaign documentation, flowcharts, budget trackers, and reporting tools that keep work organized and accurate. The position gathers audience, market, and competitive data, updates planning systems, and monitors campaign pacing, delivery, and budget utilization to help ensure media activity aligns with approved strategies and client objectives. This role also coordinates with planners, buyers, vendors, and internal teams to confirm campaign readiness, resolve discrepancies, and support billing, reconciliation, and proof-of-performance requirements. Through strong attention to detail, adherence to process standards, and continued learning of media planning fundamentals, the job contributes to reliable campaign execution, operational efficiency, and high-quality client deliverables.

**What you'll do**
==================

* **Develop media planning support materials** — Assist in the preparation and maintenance of media plans, flowcharts, authorization documents, budget tracking tools, and campaign records. Ensure planning materials are accurate, current, and organized so planners, buyers, and account teams can execute campaigns efficiently.
* **Compile audience, market, and competitive data** — Gather audience insights, market information, media consumption data, and competitive intelligence from approved sources to support planning analyses and help identify opportunities relevant to client objectives and local market conditions.
* **Maintain planning and reporting systems** — Enter, update, validate, and organize information within planning tools, spreadsheets, flowcharts, pacing reports, and media systems. Help ensure campaign data remains accurate, accessible, and aligned with approved plans and documentation standards.
* **Support campaign execution and readiness** — Partner with planners, buyers, vendors, and internal teams to confirm campaign requirements, creative assets, approvals, specifications, and launch timelines are complete and ready for execution. * **Support media budget stewardship** — Assist with invoice verification, billing documentation, reconciliation support, and budget tracking activities. * **Assist with reporting and client deliverables** — Prepare campaign summaries, delivery reports, proof-of-performance documentation, presentation materials, and other supporting resources used in client communications, stewardship meetings, and post-campaign reporting.
* **Develop media planning expertise and industry awareness** — Develop foundational knowledge of media planning principles, audience strategy, channel capabilities, campaign measurement, and integrated communications through training, observation, and participation in planning activities. Apply new knowledge and industry trends to assigned responsibilities while preparing for increased planning ownership.
* **Follow media process and quality standards** — Apply established agency procedures, documentation standards, workflow requirements, and quality-control practices to reduce errors, improve consistency, and support reliable campaign execution. jobs.title: Junior Digital Marketing Analyst
jobs.desc:
**Junior Digital Analyst**  
EOS Healthcare Marketing, Parker, Colorado

EOS Healthcare Marketing is a search and digital marketing agency based in Parker, Colorado. We’ve been helping dental, veterinary, and other healthcare practices grow for over two decades. We’re a tight-knit team of marketers and designers, and we’re looking for our next Junior Digital Analyst to join the Digital department.

This is a great fit for someone with curiosity, brains, and energy who wants to be on the front edge of what’s happening in SEO and Google Ads. You should have at least a basic understanding of digital marketing, but more than anything, we’re looking for the right person to train. A bachelor’s degree in marketing or a related field is required for this role. Recent college graduates are welcome and encouraged to apply.

**How we work, and why it matters for this role**

Digital marketing changes fast, and the last couple of years have changed it more than the ten before that. AI tools are now part of how we research keywords, write and edit content, build reports, and audit websites. Google keeps changing how search results look, and more people are getting answers from AI assistants like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google’s AI Overviews instead of clicking a list of links. We think that’s exciting, and we’ve built a lot of our day-to-day workflow around it.

That means this role isn’t about learning one set of tools and running them the same way for five years. The tools we use today will look different a year from now, and some of them haven’t been built yet. We want someone who enjoys that. You’ll be expected to try new tools, figure out what they’re good at and where they fall short, and help us decide what’s worth keeping.

We’re also thinking a lot about the bigger picture. AI is going to keep changing what marketing jobs look like, including this one. Some tasks that take hours today will take minutes, and new kinds of work will show up that nobody is doing yet. We want someone who’s genuinely interested in that question and wants to help figure out how our team adapts, not someone who’s worried about it or ignoring it. AI doesn’t replace judgment, though. You’ll also be the person checking the output, catching mistakes, and making sure what goes out to a client is accurate.

**The ideal candidate will have these traits:**

* Curious: This is the big one. You want to be out in front of what’s changing in SEO and Google Ads. You follow Google updates, read industry news, and test new ideas because you actually find it interesting, not because someone assigned it. When something new comes out, your first instinct is to dig in and figure out if it could help our clients.
* Interested in where AI is taking our industry: You think about how AI will change marketing work over the next few years, and you want to be part of shaping how our team uses it. You have opinions about it and you’re open to having them change as you learn more.

jobs.title: Junior Marketing Manager
jobs.desc:
Junior Marketing Manager

About the role

We’re looking for a creative, organized person who is comfortable with social media and knows how to use AI to work more efficiently. This is a hands-on dealership marketing role for someone with limited professional experience who wants to learn the business and grow into greater responsibility.

You’ll help bring our vehicles, people, and customer experience to life online. You don’t need years of experience managing a marketing department. We’re looking for initiative, good judgment, strong follow-through, and a willingness to learn.

Responsibilities

* Create social media content, including photos, short videos, reels, stories, and posts
* Capture vehicle walkarounds, employee features, dealership events, and customer stories with appropriate permission
* Maintain a content calendar and coordinate with sales, service, and management to highlight relevant vehicles, offers, and dealership news
* Monitor comments and messages, respond professionally, and connect customer inquiries with the appropriate team
* Assist with website updates, email campaigns, promotions, and community marketing
* Use AI tools to brainstorm ideas, draft captions, repurpose content, organize projects, and reduce time spent on repetitive tasks
* Review AI-generated work for accuracy and brand consistency, protect customer information, and obtain approval for pricing, offers, and promotional claims
* Track engagement, website traffic, and inquiries to understand what’s working and recommend improvements
* Keep marketing materials organized and follow projects through to completion

What we’re looking for

* A working knowledge of Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and current social media format
* Basic photography and video skills, including shooting on a smartphone and making simple edits
* Familiarity with tools such as ChatGPT, Canva, or CapCut, and an interest in learning new technology
* Strong writing skills, attention to detail, and good judgment about public-facing content
* Comfort working with different departments and taking initiative to find content opportunities
* The ability to write and organize SEO content that helps our sites stay relevant.
* Organization, reliability, and the ability to manage several small projects at once
* A positive response to feedback and a genuine desire to develop professionally

Experience and qualifications

Previous dealership experience is not required. Personal projects, internships, freelance work, volunteer experience, and social media accounts you’ve helped manage all count.

Growth opportunity

This position begins with hands-on content creation and day-to-day marketing execution. As you demonstrate your skills and learn the business, the role can expand into campaign planning, performance reporting and broader marketing management.
